description.narrative:
Detta beslut och tillhörande beredning avser en ny insats (Beslut om insats, Insatshanteringsregeln 2.9 §) mellan Sida och Rädda Barnens Riksförbund (Rädda Barnen) för avtalsperioden 2021-2025. Beslut och tillhörande beredningar avser dessutom stöd till Rädda Barnens humanitära verksamhet under 2021-2024 (stöd för avtalsåren 2025 är avhängligt Sidas godkännande av Rädda Barnens fullständiga ansökan för respektive år enligt att-satserna ovan). Aktuellt beslut omfattar finansiellt stöd till Rädda Barnen om 97 317 333 SEK under 2024.
Målet med insatsen (2021-2025) är att bidra till tre "Förändringar" (Breakthroughs) som identifierats inom Save the Children-rörelsen som del av dess vision för 2030. Dessa är att barn ska:
1. Överleva - inga barn dör av orsaker som kan förebyggas innan de fyllt fem år. 2. Lära - alla barn får del av kvalitativ grundläggande utbildning. 3. Vara skyddade - våld mot barn tolereras inte längre.
I ljuset av Sveriges "Strategi för Sveriges humanitära bistånd genom Styrelsen för internationellt utvecklingssamarbete (Sida) 2021-2025" kommer särskilt den tredje Förändringen - vara skyddade - att vara central, eftersom ett av strategins huvudmål är "Förbättrad förmåga att tillgodose skydd och assistans för krisdrabbade människor". Rädda Barnen kommer dessutom i hög utsträckning att integrera skyddskomponenter i sin multisektoriella assistans inom ramen för insatsens tema "Centrality of Protection". Detta tema syftar till att på ett holistiskt sätt minska skyddsrelaterade risker och svara upp mot skyddsrelaterade behov hos barn i kombination med andra projektkomponenter, snarare än att betrakta skydd som isolerat från andra delmål.

During 2020, Sida's Unit for Humanitarian Assistance conducted an overview of ongoing strategic partnerships in order to ensure that partnerships were established with the most relevant and effective humanitarian actors to carry out Sida's Humanitarian Strategy. As a result of the overview, Sida has decided to appraise a new contribution and enter into a new strategic partnership agreement with Save the Children Sweden (SCS) for the period 2021-2025 (see archive number 2021-000057).
The total initial contribution to SCS in 2024 amounts to SEK 97 317 333.
The overall objective of the intervention is to contribute to the promotion of three Breakthroughs in the way children are treated in the world: Survive, Learn and Be Protected. These are part of the Save the Children movement's Vision for 2030 and are defined as remarkable and sustainable shifts from current trends that Save the Children aspires to work to achieve for children. Their respective objective is the following:
1. Survive: No child dies of preventable causes before their fifth birthday. 2. Learn: All children learn from quality basic education. 3. Be Protected: Violence against children is no longer tolerated.
One of the main comparative advantages of Save the Children is its competence in addressing protection-related concerns. For this reason, Centrality of Protection has been proposed as the thematic frame, making the Be Protected Breakthrough particularly central for its interventions during the agreement period.
Finally, in addition to these three Breakthroughs, the proposed contribution also aligns with Sweden's newly adopted "Strategy for Sweden’s humanitarian assistance provided through the Swedish International Development Cooperation Agency (Sida) 2021–2025".

The overall objective of the intervention is to deliver lifesaving assistance and protection to crisis-affected children and adults in humanitarian situations. Save the Children will do so by contributing to the promotion of three Breakthroughs in the way children are treated in the world: Survive, Learn and Be Protected. These are part of the Save the Children movement's Vision for 2030 and are defined as remarkable and sustainable shifts from current trends that Save the Children aspires to work to achieve for children. Their respective objective is the following: Survive: No child dies of preventable causes before their fifth birthday. Learn: All children learn from quality basic education. Be Protected: Violence against children is no longer tolerated.

description.narrative:
SCS has submitted annual reports for four out of the five activity periods of the full agreement period. So far, reports are always submitted on time and are consistently assessed to be of high quality - providing aggregated results about the number of people reached with lifesaving humanitarian assistance and protection services and outcome levels results such as the improvement in psychosocial well-being, access to clean water et cetera.
Throughout the agreement period, Save the Children Sweden (SCS) has continuously been assessed by geographical programme officers at Sida's Department for Humanitarian Operations (Sida HUM) for the purposes of allocating humanitarian funding to the best-placed humanitarian actors with the best capacity to deliver principled and integrated lifesaving assistance and protection to crisis-affected people. As a result, Save the Children has been awarded a total of SEK 582,379,333 during the agreement period. Out of this total, SEK 410.5 million has been in the form of funding for annual country projects and programmes in 10 different crises, with several country offices receiving funding in multiple years due to Save the Children demonstrating quality programming and good results in supporting crisis-affected populations with lifesaving assistance and protection in an principled, effective and inclusive manner.
Moreover, SCS has been awarded SEK 137.5 million for a Rapid Response Mechanism (RRM) supported by Sida HUM that has enabled Save the Children to launch projects after severe deteriorations in humanitarian situations or following sudden-onset emergencies, including multiple earthquakes, flooding events and conflict-induced displacement. SCS has completed a total of 33 Rapid Response Mechanism (RRM) projects with Sida funding over the agreement period. Through these projects, Save the Children has been able to rapidly launch or scale up emergency interventions following sudden onset disasters or when there have been severe deteriorations in the humanitarian situation. It shall also be noted that Sida assess that SCS's decision-making when it comes for prioritising when and where to apply for RRM project funding is strategic, considering that SCS as a general rule do not apply for RRM funding in crises where they already have the flexibility of the PBA funding to scale up activities by shifting existing resources.
SCS, through Save the Children International (SCI), routinely reach the number of beneficiaries targeted in the individual project and programme documents, and are assessed to do so through the provision of integrated assistance and protection services that is of high quality.
A few additional examples to highlight from the current agreement period include:
- between 1 April 2021 and 31 March 2025, Save the Children has been able to reach 856,957 people through its annual humanitarian country projects (19 different annual country projects spread over 9 different countries) and 33 RRM projects.
- Save the Children were able to reach 5,598,023 people through its humanitarian country programmes in Haiti, Mali, Mozambique and Ukraine that Sida provided programme-based approach (PBA) funding for in 2023 and 2024. This figure represents the total reach of the humanitarian country programmes in these countries during these two years, and the activities were not exclusively covered by Sida HUM's funding but also financed by other donors. However, Sida's PBA funding is still significant in size and highly flexible. In 2024, Sida's funding represented 10, 20, 8.5 and 3 per cent of the total expenditure in Haiti, Mali, Mozambique and Ukraine, respectively.
- SCS has been able to pilot and adapt its operations to Sida's programme-based approach (PBA) funding modality, including new ways of working. Positive examples of adapting to and leveraging the flexibility of the PBA modality is how resources have been re-directed in crises to meet more urgent needs or sudden onset needs. Moreover, SCS has reported great progress from the SCI Mali country office in terms of meaningful inclusion of local partners in the decision-making process for how to most efficiently leverage the PBA funding.
- SCS has also been awarded funding to strengthen its capacity and to developed new methods and ways of working within several areas of work, including in strengthening local leadership in humanitarian action, access negotiations to hard-to-reach areas and in advancing Centrality of Protection. Two recently concluded method and capacity development projects for advancing Anticipatory Action will be reported to Sida in September 2026 but SCS has indicated that the lessons learned from these projects have been well-received among SCI country offices.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
